'''James E. Gentle''' (born 1943) is an American statistician and author. He was a professor of statistics at [[George Mason University]] until his retirement in 2016. He is Co-Editor-in-Chief of [[Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews: Computational Statistics]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wires.wiley.com/WileyCDA/Section/id-398002.html?al=eb|title= Editorial Board}}</ref> and Senior Editor of [[Communications in Statistics]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Editorial Board|journal=Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation|volume=41|issue=10|pages=ebi|doi=10.1080/03610918.2012.703092|year=2012|s2cid=218568509}}</ref>

Gentle has written nine books, several book chapters and many research papers. His research is focused on statistical computing, simulation, robust statistics, survey sampling, and computational finance.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n80013746/|title= WorldCat: Gentle, James E.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/matrix-algebra-theory-computations-and-applications-in-statistics|title= Matrix Algebra: Theory, Computations, and Applications in Statistics}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2004/20_Fellows.pdf |title= AAAS Fellows}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]]. He is an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.buecher.de/shop/analysis/elements-of-computational-statistics/gentle-james-e-/products_products/detail/prod_id/32191300/|title=Elements of Computational Statistics}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Gentle was born in [[Statesville, North Carolina]]. He received a B.S in Mathematics from [[University of North Carolina]] in 1966 followed by an M.C.S in Computer Science in 1973 and a Ph.D. in Statistics in 1974 from [[Texas A&M University]] under the supervision of [[Herman Otto Hartley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stat.tamu.edu/about/awards-and-prizes/h-o-hartley-award/|title=H.O. Hartley Award}}</ref>

== Career ==
Right after completing his Ph.D, Gentle joined the [[Iowa State University]] as an assistant professor of statistics. He was given tenure as an associate professor in 1978. A year later, he left Iowa State University to join IMSL, Inc., as the director of research and design.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Editorial Collaborators|journal = The American Statistician|volume = 42|issue = 4|pages = 294–296|jstor = 2685153|year = 1988}}</ref> In 1992, Gentle left [[IMSL Numerical Libraries|IMSL]] and joined George Mason University as university professor of computational statistics. During his career at Iowa State and George Mason, Gentle supervised 22 PhD dissertations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mason.gmu.edu/~jgentle/|title= James Gentle}}</ref>

In 1997, Gentle began a two-year leave from George Mason to serve as a program director in the Division of Mathematical Sciences of the [[National Science Foundation]].
 
He has been a visiting professor at Texas A&M University, [[University of Texas at Dallas]], [[Rice University]], [[University of Texas at Arlington]], and [[Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)|Harbin Institute of Technology Shenzhen Graduate School]].

Throughout his career, Gentle has been active in the American Statistical Association,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2015/02/01/lifetimemembers_2015/ |title=Recognizing the ASA's Lifetime Members|date=February 2015 }}</ref> more specifically the Statistical Computing Section and the Statistical Graphics Section.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stat-computing.org/computing/officers/1991.html|title= Statistical Computing - Statistical Graphics - 1991}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stat-computing.org/newsletter/issues/scgn-15-1.pdf|title= JSM 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stat-computing.org/computing/officers/1993.html |title= Statistical Computing - Statistical Graphics - 1993}}</ref>

== Books ==
=== As an author ===
*''Statistical Computing'' (with W. J. Kennedy,1980)
*''Numerical Linear Algebra with Applications in Statistics'' (1998)
*''Elements of Computational Statistics'' (2002)
*''Random Number Generation and Monte Carlo Methods'' (2003)
*''Computational Statistics'' (2009)
*''Statistical Analysis of Financial Data'' (2020)
*''Gentle Cooking'' (2023)
*''Buen Provecho. Favorite Recipes from South of the Border --- and Beyond'' (2023)
*''Matrix Algebra. Theory, Computations, and Applications in Statistics'' (2024)

=== As an editor===
*''Computer Science and Statistics: Proceedings of the Fifteenth Symposium on the Interface'' (1983)
*''Handbook of Computational Finance'' (2012)
*''Handbook of Computational Statistics'' (2012)
